findings: The paired overview pages retain the same general bank-debit flow: merchant can pull from a customer's bank account for one-time or recurring purchases after the customer supplies bank details and grants a debit mandate; some routes use microdeposits or bank-login verification, and traditional bank-debit confirmation can take several business days (old raw lines 8-23; new raw lines 9-24). Mandate authorization, optional verification, PaymentIntent confirmation and funds availability are distinct states; the three-step illustration is not a promise of immediate payment completion. The overview cautions immediate-delivery and dispute-sensitive businesses rather than prohibiting all such use (old raw lines 13-16; new raw lines 14-17).

The one substantive product-table delta is the combined 'Instant Bank Payments or ACH Direct Debit' row's Mobile Payment Element mark changing from supported in May to unsupported in November, with its other product marks stable (old raw lines 29-36, especially line 31; new raw lines 30-37, especially line 32; diff lines 16-31). The row names two methods but does not split the mobile mark by method, so the captures do not establish which path changed or whether a merchant's platform/runtime support was removed. The dedicated May Instant Bank Payments raw still lists Mobile Payment Element at raw/stripe-instant-bank-payments-2025.md lines 123-129, echoed by source-stripe-instant-bank-payments.md line 21 and concept stripe-instant-bank-payments.md line 41; retain that as dated authority and add a reciprocal disagreement warning, not a silent overwrite.

The API table remains method-specific and materially unchanged: ACH us_bank_account supports PaymentIntents, SetupIntents and setup_future_usage but not manual capture; Bacs bacs_debit has a SetupIntent table unsupported mark with a Checkout setup-mode footnote, and its PaymentIntent confirmation requires a Stripe-owned-flow mandate (old raw lines 44-53; new raw lines 45-54). AU BECS, NZ BECS, ACSS and SEPA have their own enum/SetupIntent rows; all six table rows mark manual capture unsupported and redirect 'No' (old raw lines 44-53; new raw lines 45-54). This ACH API row is not an API-support statement for Link Instant Bank Payments, which is only paired with ACH in the product table (old raw lines 29-31, 44-46; new raw lines 30-32, 45-47).

Bacs' table footnotes must be read as route-specific qualifications: Payment Element cannot create Bacs SetupIntents, Checkout setup mode can create them, and PaymentIntent confirmation works after a Mandate from Checkout, Payment Element or Payment Links (old raw lines 38, 47, 53; new raw lines 39, 48, 54). ACSS/Canadian PADs exclude Payment Links and Mobile Payment Element in the product table, Checkout subscription mode and deferred-intent creation in footnotes; those limits are unchanged despite the now-updated quickstart link (old raw lines 35, 38, 50, 53; new raw lines 36, 39, 51, 54). A displayed ✓ or dashboard setting does not establish a particular merchant's eligibility, mandate collection or completed debit.

Current source-stripe-bank-debits.md retains May-only provenance and accurately lists the six API enums, no manual capture in those six API rows, Bacs and ACSS exceptions (source lines 4-8, 15-41; old raw lines 29-53; new raw lines 30-54). It misses the new combined-row Mobile Payment Element conflict. Its line 13 'Confirmation takes several business days' and line 28 'No manual capture support' are overbroad if applied to Instant Bank Payments: the older dedicated Link method page documents immediate confirmation and manual capture (raw/stripe-instant-bank-payments-2025.md lines 4-10, 48-58, 105-107). Source line 19 combines ACH and IBP in one method/enum row, but us_bank_account belongs to the ACH API row, not a demonstrated IBP API identity (old raw lines 29-31, 44-47; new raw lines 30-32, 45-48). Narrow these source statements to the listed debit API methods and distinguish Link IBP with dated provider-specific authority.

The migration advice is unchanged: existing Sources, Tokens or Bank Accounts integrations are advised to follow the ACH-specific or general guide toward Payment Intents, rather than the page proving migration has occurred (old raw lines 55-60; new raw lines 56-61). New raw changes to an external flow SVG URL, Bacs link target, ACSS quickstart link, table formatting, italics and heading spacing are presentation/navigation changes, not new mandate, eligibility or settlement rules (diff lines 3-15, 16-66). The source can add November provenance while keeping May historical wording and the mobile-mark disagreement.

Because it is a combined row and the dedicated May IBP guide says Mobile Payment Element supported, record the dated documentation disagreement without assigning a precise method or inferring live removal (raw/stripe-instant-bank-payments-2025.md lines 123-129).

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bank-debits, the November overview describes mandate-authorized pulls from a customer's bank account for one-time or recurring purchases, sometimes with pre-payment microdeposit or bank-login verification; traditional bank debits can take several business days to confirm and may favor customers in disputes (new raw lines 9-24). Product support is a table by method and UI, while the API table separately lists six debit enums and modal Bacs mandate/Checkout setup and Canadian PAD route restrictions (new raw lines 26-54). A mandate, verification or displayed product mark is not a completed debit or payout. The May overview had the same general flow and API constraints (old raw lines 8-23, 25-53), but its combined Instant Bank Payments/ACH Mobile Payment Element cell was supported where November says unsupported (old raw line 31; new raw line 32). source-stripe-bank-debits.md captures the six enums and exceptions but lacks that dated difference and overgeneralizes multi-day confirmation and no manual capture across Link Instant Bank Payments (source lines 13-35; dedicated May IBP raw lines 4-10, 48-58).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bank-debits, the substantive documentation delta is the combined Instant Bank Payments-or-ACH Direct Debit Mobile Payment Element cell changing from supported to unsupported; it cannot be assigned to one of the two methods or treated as proven live removal (old raw line 31; new raw line 32). The dedicated May IBP page, source and concept still list Mobile Payment Element supported, so source-stripe-bank-debits.md and the IBP route need reciprocal dated warnings (raw/stripe-instant-bank-payments-2025.md lines 123-129; source-stripe-instant-bank-payments.md line 21; concept stripe-instant-bank-payments.md line 41). Separate baseline source defects are blanket multi-day confirmation/no-manual-capture and a combined ACH/IBP us_bank_account label, because the API row belongs to ACH while Link IBP's dedicated page says instant confirmation and manual capture supported (old raw lines 29-31, 44-47; new raw lines 30-32, 45-47). The flow SVG URL, Bacs link target, ACSS quickstart link, table spacing and italics are presentational/navigation changes (diff lines 3-66). Preserve May provenance and method-specific mandate/Checkout setup, delayed-versus-instant confirmation, eligibility and client-route distinctions; neither a table checkmark, mandate, redirect note nor PaymentIntent creation proves final payment, funds availability or account access.
